chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is it for the man to marry the Christian woman upon the Muslim woman, and the slave girl upon the free woman? He said: No. One of the two (the Christian or the slave) is not married upon the Muslim woman, but the Muslim woman is married upon the slave girl and the Christian woman; and for the Muslim woman is two-thirds, and for the slave girl and the Christian woman is one-third.

key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّةُ: Christian woman (specifically from the People of the Book)

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy and time distribution for a Muslim man's wives if he has a Muslim, Christian, and slave wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchical precedence in polygyny, establishing that a free Muslim wife holds priority over both a slave girl and a Christian (Kitabi) wife, who are considered equal in status. It specifies the division of time, granting the Muslim wife two-thirds of the husband's attention while the slave and Christian wives share the remaining third. This ruling reflects the classical Shia juristic view on the social and legal stratification of wives based on freedom, faith, and lineage.
